chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr). He said: 'It is the night of the twenty-first or the twenty-third.' I said: 'Is it not only one night?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then inform me which one it is.' He said: 'What does it matter to you if you do good in both nights?'

key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Decree, a highly virtuous night in Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Laylat al-Qadr being one night or two according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the scholarly debate regarding the precise date of Laylat al-Qadr, confirming it as either the 21st or 23rd of Ramadan. He employs a principle of *takhayyur* (choice) to alleviate the anxiety of uncertainty, advising that performing worship on both nights ensures the reward of the single, specific night. This reflects the Shia emphasis on maximizing devotion during the odd nights of Ramadan while acknowledging the hidden nature of the exact date.
